name: Olanzapine
summary: A highly effective atypical antipsychotic with the heaviest metabolic burden of the class — weight gain, diabetes, and dyslipidemia.
mechanism: Antagonizes D2 and 5-HT2A receptors plus H1, muscarinic, and 5-HT2C receptors — a broad receptor profile.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Antipsychotic effect over days–weeks; sedation within hours

dosing.adult: 5–10 mg once daily (schizophrenia/mania); 2.5–5 mg in agitation contexts

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; third-trimester exposure can cause neonatal EPS or withdrawal; gestational weight gain is a concern.
safety.lactation: Present in breast milk; limited data.
warnings: Boxed warning (antipsychotics): increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
Metabolic syndrome — weight gain, hyperglycemia/diabetes, and dyslipidemia (prominent)
safety.overdose: Sedation, anticholinergic effects, and hypotension; coma possible at large doses.

clinicalPearls: Smoking induces CYP1A2 — olanzapine levels rise (and sedation increases) after smoking cessation.
Among the most effective antipsychotics, but metabolic monitoring is mandatory — screen glucose and lipids.
good: Severe psychosis or mania where efficacy and sedation are priorities.
bad: Metabolic risk (obesity, diabetes, dyslipidemia) and patients who must avoid weight gain.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard psychopharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
